battle.name: 高盧戰爭
battle.brief: 前58年凱撒以山南高盧總督之位北進，先後打垮赫爾維蒂人、貝爾蓋人、維納提人與越萊茵河的日耳曼援軍，前52年在阿萊西亞合圍維欽托利。卡面這名羅馬重步兵站在軍團縱隊裡，靠方盾、短劍與標槍撐起整條戰線。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 高盧戰爭（前58年至前50年）是羅馬共和國對高盧各部族發動的一連串征伐，同時也是把義大利的軍制帶到萊茵河與泰晤士河下游的一次遠征。開戰的一方是羅馬共和國：元老院授權前58年的山南高盧總督尤利烏斯·凱撒全權指揮，麾下有公民兵團十個大隊（每團約四千八百至六千人）、拉丁同盟與義大利同盟的徵召兵，以及盟邦提供的輔兵——標槍手、弓箭手、投石手與騎兵；第十軍團「雲雀」甚至直接在高盧境內徵募高盧青年，成為第一支非公民的軍團。另一方是鬆散的高盧世界：南方的阿基坦人、西部的凱爾特高盧（阿爾維爾尼、艾杜伊、塞格納尼、圖倫戈、帕里西等）、北部的貝爾蓋人、西部海岸的維納提人與雷迪人；戰事中又有萊茵東岸的日耳曼人蘇維匯人隨阿里奧維斯圖斯越境支援，以及不列顛島上以卡西維拉努斯為首的部族聯盟。這些陣營並非全程結盟：前61年納博訥被羅馬攻破後，阿洛布羅吉人與阿爾維爾尼人逃入羅馬行省求助，才讓凱撒得到開戰的藉口；前57年貝爾蓋人與高盧中部各打各的，互不相救；前52年維欽托利才把散處的部落組織成一個聯盟，才有了這場戰爭真正的正面對決。
countriesEn: The Gallic Wars (58–50 BC) were a series of Roman campaigns against the tribes of Gaul, and at the same time an expedition that carried the Italian military system to the Rhine and to the lower Thames. On one side stood the Roman Republic: the Senate had authorised a single commander, Gaius Julius Caesar, who held the governorship of Cisalpine and Transalpine Gaul from 58 BC. Under him marched ten legions of Roman citizens (roughly four thousand eight hundred to six thousand men each), levies of the Latin League and of the Italian allies, and auxiliaries provided by the allied states — javelin-men, archers, slingers and cavalry. The Tenth Legion, the Alaudae, was even recruited inside Gaul and became the first non-citizen legion Rome ever fielded. On the other side lay a loose Gallic world: the Aquitani in the south, the Celtic Gauls of the centre and west (the Arverni, Aedui, Sequani, Turones, Parisii and the rest), the Belgae of the north, and on the Atlantic coast the Veneti and the Redones; in the course of the war the Suebi under Ariovistus crossed the Rhine to intervene, and on the island of Britain there was the confederation headed by Cassivellaunus. These camps were never allied for the whole war. After the fall of Narbo in 61 BC the Allobroges and the Arverni fled into the Roman province and asked for help, and that gave Caesar his pretext. In 57 BC the Belgae and the central Gauls fought their own separate wars and gave each other no aid. It was only in 52 BC, under Vercingetorix, that the scattered tribes were organised into one coalition, and that was the real face-to-face contest of this war.
people: 凱撒是貫穿全程的唯一一人，也是這場戰爭的政治動機所在：他以山南高盧總督的身分出戰，既要替羅馬開疆，也要在前三頭同盟的框架裡壓過龐培的西班牙戰線，並用高盧的戰功換取延長執政權。羅馬方面的將領與幕僚包括他的內政副手提圖斯·拉比埃努斯、第十軍團「雲雀」的老兵、騎兵指揮官馬克·安東尼、昆圖斯·圖利烏斯·西塞羅（被安比奧里克斯包圍，靠援軍解圍）、小克拉蘇、布魯圖·阿爾比努、蓋烏斯·特萊包涅斯，以及在不列顛戰役中陣亡的薩比努斯與科塔兩位指揮官；元老院那邊則有執政官比布盧斯與護民官瓦提尼烏斯的拖延，以及克拉蘇與龐培在背後撐腰。高盧方面的關鍵人物同樣鮮明：維欽托利把西部與南部各部拉成聯盟，用游擊與圍城拖住凱撒，最後在阿萊西亞丟下佩劍；安比奧里克斯在東北方全殲羅馬駐軍；阿里奧維斯圖斯帶日耳曼人越萊茵河而來，打完卻自居高盧盟主，勒索人質與土地；科密烏斯守土倫，是唯一守到最後的部族領袖；卡西維拉努斯在不列顛以輕戰車與騎兵打游擊，最後在城中被圍投降；曼德布拉修斯因王位被奪而引凱撒入島，反過來被中世紀的威爾士史家罵作凱爾特人的恥辱。
peopleEn: Caesar is the one man who runs through the whole war, and he is also its political motive. He went out as governor of Transalpine Gaul in order to extend Roman territory, to outdo Pompey, who was fighting the Spanish war, within the framework of the First Triumvirate, and to convert Gallic victories into an extension of his own command. His lieutenants and subordinates in Rome's service included his administrative second, Titus Labienus, the veterans of the Tenth Legion, the cavalry commander Mark Antony, Quintus Tullius Cicero (who was surrounded by Ambiorix and relieved by the marching column), the younger Crassus, Brutus Albinus and Gaius Trebonius, and the two commanders killed in the British campaigns, Sabinus and Cotta. On the senate's side there were the dilatoriness of the consuls Bibulus and the tribune Vatinius, with Crassus and Pompey backing Caesar from behind. The Gallic figures are equally vivid. Vercingetorix tied the tribes of the west and south into a coalition, wore Caesar down with harassment and sieges, and finally threw down his sword at Alesia. Ambiorix annihilated a Roman garrison in the north-east. Ariovistus came across the Rhine with German troops, won, and then set himself up as lord of Gaul, pressing for hostages and land. Commius, who held the town of Tours, was the only tribal leader to hold out to the end. Cassivellaunus fought a running war of light chariots and cavalry in Britain and finally surrendered in his own besieged town. Mandubracius, robbed of his kingship, guided Caesar onto the island, and for that betrayal the medieval Welsh chroniclers branded him a disgrace of the Celts.
kits: 卡面這名羅馬重步兵是前100年前後的編制：頭戴蒙提式青銅盔，盔脊兩側焊死護頰，頸甲只有一小片；身上穿的是鎖子甲或皮札甲，不是分段甲——分段甲要到奧古斯都時代才取代它；左手握橢圓形大盾，盾面彎曲以貼合臂彎，右手是西班牙式短劍，刃長約五十公分，刺多於劈；腰後別一把匕首，肩後插兩支標槍，槍身約兩米四、槍頭與柄鑄成一體並以鉛加重。整套裝備的邏輯是「洗臉」：先用標槍在五十步內打亂敵人陣形，再上短劍收割。與他並列的還有羅馬的投射兵器與攻城器材——野戰弩炮、投石砲、柴扉（推到城牆下的防禦棚）、柴束、填壕用的柵籬、可移動的高台與吊橋，騎兵則用短劍與投槍。高盧方面：中部與南部部族用雙刃長劍、長矛、投槍與小圓盾，北方貝爾蓋人擅長以鐵鏈與砍刀貼身纏鬥，西部維納提人另有數百艘橡木海船，舷牆高約兩公尺、船底寬平，能在潮汐洶湧的海灣裡撞擊羅馬的傳輸船。糧食與運輸是另一套裝備：赫爾維蒂人靠牛群與大篷車隊遷徙，羅馬則靠義大利與西班牙的穀物、馬薩利亞的港口與新修的軍用道路維持遠征。
kitsEn: The legionary on the card belongs to the order of about 100 BC. He wears a Montefortino-style bronze helmet with the cheek-pieces permanently welded to the bowl and only a short neck guard; on his body is chain mail or a leather jerkin, not segmented plate, which only replaced it in the age of Augustus. His left hand grips the large oval scutum, its face curved to fit the arm, his right holds the Spanish gladius, about fifty centimetres of blade, built to thrust rather than to cut; a dagger rides at his belt and two javelins stand behind his shoulder, each about two metres and forty long, the shaft and head cast in one piece and weighted with lead. The logic of the whole set is to wash the enemy: first break his formation with the pilum inside fifty paces, then reap him with the sword. Alongside this man stand Rome's missile weapons and siege tools — field ballistae and stone-throwers, the vinea shed pushed up against a wall, fascines, the ramp of hurdle-work filled into ditches, movable towers and drawbridges — and the cavalry, with their short swords and javelins. The Gauls of the centre and south carried double-edged longswords, long spears, throwing javelins and small round shields; the Belgae of the north were expert at closing with chain-swords and chopping blades; and the Veneti of the west had several hundred oak-built ships with rails about two metres high and wide flat bottoms, able to ram the Roman transports in a tidally confused bay. Food and transport formed another set of equipment: the Helvetii moved with herds and covered wagon trains, while Rome kept the expedition supplied with grain from Italy and Spain, the harbour of Massalia, and newly built military roads.
tactics: 這場戰爭留下兩套完整的戰術記錄。一套是凱撒的羅馬軍：以營地為軸，每夜挖壕立柵；接戰時分三線，最前是散兵投標槍與騷擾，後面是主力中隊，最後是預備隊；進攻時密集的投槍陣一次拋出三排標槍，然後以盾牆接近，短劍近戰，危急時收成龜甲陣。圍城是另一門本領：在阿萊西亞，羅馬繞城築起約二十四公里的環形圍牆，牆外挖壕、埋樁、設木柵，牆上立十五座土木堡壘，堡壘之間再拉起反向圍牆攔截援軍；高盧人則在城牆上堆土築台抵擋投石，並挖地道反制。另一套是高盧與日耳曼的戰術：赫爾維蒂人把老弱與車隊放在中軍、步兵護住兩翼；內爾維人善用林地斜坡伏擊，密集突進到貼身距離，薩比斯河一役幾乎吃掉羅馬兩翼，靠的正是標槍射程之外的近戰；貝爾蓋人善守多角形的山城，每個角上都築土壘。維欽托利則把游擊、斷糧與圍城合用：避開凱撒的主力與會戰，分兵襲擊其交通線，逼羅馬分兵，最後在阿萊西亞用全軍硬撼羅馬經營的圍城線——這是唯一一次高盧人正面進攻羅馬經營的圍城工事。
tacticsEn: The war left two complete sets of tactical records. The first is Caesar's Roman army. Its axis was the camp: every night a ditch was dug and a rampart raised; in battle it deployed in three lines, skirmishers throwing the pilum and working the enemy in front, the main body of cohorts behind them, and the reserves last. On the attack a dense javelin line loosed three ranks of pila, the line then closed behind shields, the sword did the killing, and when pressed the files closed into a testudo. Siege work was a second discipline of its own: at Alesia the Romans ran a ring of circumvallation about twenty-four kilometres around the town, with a ditch, driven stakes and a timber palisade outside it, fifteen turf-and-timber redoubts on the wall itself, and a line of contravallation between the redoubts to intercept relief; the Gauls countered by piling earth on the rampart to blunt the stone-throwers and by digging tunnels. The second set belongs to the Gauls and Germans. The Helvetii put the old, the women and the wagons in the middle with infantry covering the flanks. The Nervii were masters of the ambush in wooded slopes, closing to stabbing distance — at the Sabis they very nearly swallowed both wings of the Roman army, precisely because they came in inside the range of the javelin. The Belgae were good at holding polygonal hill towns, with a rampart at every angle. Vercingetorix combined harassment, cutting of supply and siege: he avoided Caesar's main body and pitched battles, struck the lines of communication to force the Romans to disperse, and finally at Alesia threw the whole Gallic coalition against Caesar's finished circumvallation — the only occasion on which the Gauls assaulted a Roman siege line head on.
data: 留下數字的地方主要是凱撒自己的《高盧戰記》與現代學者的推算。兵員方面：前58年羅馬方面約六個軍團，兩萬四千至三萬人，高盧一側兩萬至五萬人（其中逾八千是隨軍家屬）；前57年羅馬增至八個軍團，約三萬二千至四萬人；前55年入不列顛時只帶兩個軍團，約一萬人；前54年第二次登島為五個軍團約二萬五千人加二千輔兵；前53年十個軍團，四萬至五萬人；前52年阿萊西亞之役，羅馬十一個軍團加一萬以上輔兵，約六萬至七萬五千人，對面高盧聯軍估計七萬至十萬人。傷亡方面，較可靠的推算是羅馬方面陣亡三萬以上、受傷一萬以上；高盧方面的當代說法極為誇張——普魯塔克與阿庇安說有百萬凱爾特人戰死、百萬被俘為奴、八百座城鎮被毀，凱撒則稱有四十三萬日耳曼人戰死，海尼格等史家認為這些數字都不可信。行程與工期：赫爾維蒂人的遷徙約走三個月，凱撒在日內瓦湖至汝拉山之間修的阻牆約十九羅里（約三十公里）；萊茵河橋兩端的營地相距二十三羅里，橋築在敵營下游十二羅里處；阿萊西亞的環形圍牆約二十四公里、十五座堡壘；維納提人出動約六百艘船。整場戰爭從前58年打到前50年，橫跨八年。
dataEn: The numbers come mainly from Caesar's own Commentaries on the Gallic War and from modern reconstructions. On strength: in 58 BC Rome had about six legions, twenty-four to thirty thousand men, against twenty to fifty thousand on the Gallic side, of whom more than eight thousand were family members carried along; in 57 BC Rome rose to eight legions, some thirty-two to forty thousand men; for the crossing to Britain in 55 BC Caesar took only two legions, about ten thousand men; the second landing in 54 BC was five legions, roughly twenty-five thousand, with two thousand auxiliaries; in 53 BC there were ten legions, forty to fifty thousand men; at Alesia in 52 BC Rome had eleven legions and more than ten thousand auxiliaries, some sixty to seventy-five thousand men, against a Gallic coalition estimated at seventy to a hundred thousand. On losses the more reliable figure is that the Romans lost over thirty thousand dead and over ten thousand wounded; the contemporary claims for the Gallic side are plainly inflated — Plutarch and Appian give a million Celts killed, a million enslaved and eight hundred towns destroyed, while Caesar claims four hundred and thirty thousand Germans killed, and historians such as Henige hold that none of the ancient numbers can be trusted. On distances and durations: the Helvetian migration took about three months to walk; the barrier Caesar built between the Lake of Geneva and the Jura ran about nineteen Roman miles, roughly thirty kilometres; the camps at the two ends of his Rhine bridge stood twenty-three miles apart, with the bridge itself twelve miles below the enemy camp; the circumvallation at Alesia was about twenty-four kilometres long with fifteen redoubts; and the Veneti put about six hundred ships to sea. The war as a whole ran from 58 to 50 BC, eight years across.
cause: 打起來有兩條互相咬合的線索。線索一在高盧：赫爾維蒂人因人口壓力、土地不足與氏族糾紛，決定整族遷往新土地，約三十萬人帶著家當上路，而羅馬正擋在他們要通過的山南高盧通道上；羅馬此前已藉「保護盟友艾杜伊人」為由拒絕借道，衝突因此不可避免。線索二在羅馬：前60年凱撒、龐培、克拉蘇組成前三頭同盟，三人各掌一方向的軍權，凱撒分到高盧，龐培分到西班牙，克拉蘇分到東方；元老院對無限擴張仍有戒心，但高盧被視為潛在的穀物與稅收來源，願意支持凱撒帶回戰利品、奴隸與土地。於是凱撒把每一次高盧部族的求援都當成擴張的理由：前61年納博訥之役打垮阿洛布羅吉人與阿爾維爾尼人，前58年藉赫爾維蒂人遷徙開戰，前57年主動打進貝爾蓋人的地盤，前56年以使節被扣為由鎮壓維納提人，前55年兩度越萊茵河打日耳曼人並兩度登陸不列顛。到前52年，擔心被逐個征服的高盧部族才在維欽托利領導下聯合起來，才有了這場戰爭真正的正面對決。
causeEn: Two interlocking threads explain why the war came about. The first lies in Gaul: pressed by population, shortage of land and disputes within the tribes, the Helvetii decided on migration as a whole people, some three hundred thousand souls moving with their households, and Rome stood directly across the corridor of Transalpine Gaul through which they meant to pass. Rome had already refused passage on the pretext of protecting its ally the Aedui, and collision became unavoidable. The second thread lies in Rome. In 60 BC Caesar, Pompey and Crassus formed the First Triumvirate and divided the military commands between them: Caesar took Gaul, Pompey Spain, Crassus the East. The Senate remained wary of endless expansion, but Gaul was seen as a potential source of grain and taxation, and the ruling class was willing to back Caesar in the hope of booty, slaves and land coming home. So Caesar turned every Gallic appeal for help into a reason to expand: the capture of Narbo in 61 BC broke the Allobroges and the Arverni; the Helvetian migration gave him his war in 58 BC; in 57 BC he struck into Belgian territory uninvited; in 56 BC the detention of his envoys gave him the Veneti; in 55 BC he crossed the Rhine twice against the Germans and put ashore in Britain twice. Only in 52 BC, when tribes afraid of being conquered one by one came together under Vercingetorix, was the real face-to-face contest of this war fought.
impact: 高盧戰爭的後果，一半在軍制，一半在羅馬的政治結構。軍制上，羅馬把圍城術制度化：環形圍牆、反向圍牆、投射砲壘與野戰營壘成為可複製的標準動作；輔兵不再是雜兵而是編制的一部分；第十軍團的徵募顯示帝國兵役的雛形；羅馬騎兵與輕裝步兵在高盧戰場上第一次系統地與重步兵協同作戰。行政上，前51年羅馬把高盧正式分成三個行省：貝爾加、里昂與新劃出的阿基坦，連同原有的山南高盧行省與沿海的布列塔尼，形成高盧總督區；城市取得公民權，道路、造幣與稅制鋪開，羅馬拉丁語逐步取代高盧語。政治上，凱撒靠戰利品與榮譽在十年裡積累出十一個軍團、一支完全聽命於自己的私人軍隊，前50年任期屆滿時他靠這支軍隊拒絕交出指揮權，前49年越過盧比孔河，內戰隨即開打，共和國的崩解由此加速。文化上，八卷《高盧戰記》既是戰報也是政治文本，它確立的凱撒式拉丁散文，後來成為西塞羅的對照面；而戰利品也進了羅馬的硬幣與私人炫耀，說明這場戰爭真正收穫的不是土地，而是可以帶回意大利的軍力。
impactEn: The consequences of the Gallic Wars are half military and half structural in the politics of Rome. On the military side Rome institutionalised siege warfare: the circumvallation, the contravallation, the artillery redoubts and the marching camp became repeatable standard practice; auxiliaries stopped being auxiliaries and became part of the order of battle; the recruiting of the Tenth Legion pointed the way to an imperial army of subject soldiers; and Roman cavalry and light infantry worked systematically alongside the heavy infantry for the first time on a Gallic battlefield. Administratively, in 51 BC Rome formally divided Gaul into three provinces — Gallia Belgica, Gallia Lugdunensis and the newly marked out Gallia Aquitania — and, with the older province of Narbonensis and the coast of Brittany, created the command of the Three Gauls. Cities received citizenship, roads, coinage and taxation spread, and Latin displaced the Gallic tongue. Politically, Caesar turned booty and honour into eleven legions and a private army wholly obedient to him; when his term expired in 50 BC he used that army to refuse to surrender his command, crossed the Rubicon in 49 BC, and the civil war followed, accelerating the dissolution of the Republic. Culturally, the eight books of the Commentaries on the Gallic War are at once a report of operations and a political text, and the plain Caesarian Latin they established later served Cicero as a foil; the booty also flowed into Roman coinage and Roman display, which shows that what this war really yielded was not land but military force that could be carried home to Italy.
result: 結局在阿萊西亞。前52年秋天，維欽托利的大軍反過來圍攻羅馬的環形工事卻攻不下來，糧盡援絕之下，他走下山坡向凱撒投降，把武器丟在凱撒腳下；凱撒在城中慶功，之後派軍掃平殘餘抵抗。前51年，已經解除武裝的維欽托利被處決，是全戰役最刺眼的一筆；阿特雷巴特人、卡杜西人、莫里尼人先後起義，皆被平定，至前51年高盧全境歸入羅馬。戰爭在形式上止於前50年：凱撒的執政官任期屆滿，帶著十一個軍團返回意大利，過了盧比孔河，內戰取代了對外征服，羅馬共和國的末路由此開始。軍功方面，凱撒用高盧的戰利品、俘獲的奴隸與金銀鑄成帶有高盧戰利品圖案的硬幣，貼在自己的頭像旁。學界通常把《高盧戰記》劃為三次戰役——前58至前57年的赫爾維蒂與貝爾蓋之役、前55至前52年的日耳曼與不列顛之役，以及前52至前50年的起義鎮壓之役；而第八卷寫的是羅馬怎樣在冬營裡把高盧人的抵抗碾平。高盧自此成為羅馬的行省，這才是這場戰爭真正的收成。
resultEn: The end came at Alesia. In the autumn of 52 BC the Gallic host under Vercingetorix turned and assaulted Caesar's circumvallation, and could not break it; with food running short and no relief coming, he came down the slope and surrendered to Caesar, throwing his weapons at the victor's feet. Caesar celebrated inside the town and then sent columns to clear the remaining resistance. In 51 BC the unarmed Vercingetorix was executed, the sharpest single entry in the ledger of the war; the Atrebates, the Cadurci and the Morini rose in turn and were put down, and by the end of 51 BC all Gaul was in Roman hands. In form the war closed in 50 BC: Caesar's term as consul expired, he marched back to Italy with his eleven legions, crossed the Rubicon, and civil war replaced foreign conquest, beginning the last phase of the Roman Republic. In terms of credit, Caesar struck coin from the booty of Gaul, the slaves and the gold and silver, and set the image of Gallic spoils beside his own portrait. Scholars usually divide the Commentaries into three wars — the Helvetian and Belgian war of 58–57 BC, the German and British war of 55–52 BC, and the war of the suppressed revolt from 52 to 50 BC — and the eighth book describes how Rome ground down Gallic resistance from its winter camps. Gaul became a province of Rome: that was the true yield of this war.
